lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Amos announces for each of Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Ammon, Moab and Judah that for three transgressions, and for four, the LORD will not turn away punishment, naming the crime and sending fire.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some nations in Amos 1-2 and say what pattern each oracle follows?
ev: Name some of the nations and a crime named for each
Notice that Judah is included (2:4-5)

nodes.d: Amos, a herdman of Tekoa, sees words concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah and Jeroboam: judgment on the nations and on Israel, five visions, and a closing promise to raise David's fallen tabernacle and restore Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who Amos was and what his book says about Israel in a few sentences?
ev: Outline: nations (1-2), sermons on Israel (3-6), visions (7-9)
Say what Amos was before the LORD sent him (1:1, 7:14-15)

nodes.t: Judgment on Israel's oppression and ingratitude
nodes.d: The LORD charges Israel with selling the righteous and the poor, profaning his name and silencing prophets, after he destroyed the Amorite and brought them out of Egypt; no strong or swift man will escape.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Israel is charged with in Amos 2:6-16 and what the LORD had done for them?
ev: List the sins in 2:6-8 and 2:12
Recall the LORD's acts for them in 2:9-11

nodes.d: Because the LORD knew Israel alone of all the families of the earth, he will punish them for their iniquities; the prophet speaks because the LORD has spoken, and the palaces and altars of Bethel will fall.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Amos 3:2 connects the LORD's knowing of Israel with punishment?
ev: Read 3:2 and say why it comes before punishment
Explain 3:7 in your own words
Describe the coming judgment in 3:11-15

nodes.t: Kine of Bashan; yet ye have not returned
nodes.d: Amos rebukes the kine of Bashan in Samaria who oppress the poor and mocks empty worship at Bethel and Gilgal; the LORD lists famine, drought, blight, plague and overthrow after which they have not returned, and calls Israel to prepare to meet God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the refrain of Amos 4:6-11 and what the LORD calls Israel to do in 4:12?
ev: List the disasters of 4:6-11 and the refrain
Say what Israel is told in 4:12

nodes.d: Amos laments for fallen Israel, tells them to seek the LORD and not Bethel, condemns those who trample the poor and pervert justice, warns that the day of the LORD is darkness, and says the LORD hates their feasts but wants justice to roll like water.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD says about Israel's feasts and songs and what he wants instead in Amos 5:21-24?
ev: Explain why the day of the LORD is darkness in 5:18-20
Describe what the LORD wants in 5:21-24

nodes.d: Amos pronounces woe on the comfortable leaders of Zion and Samaria who lie on ivory beds and feast but are not grieved for Joseph's affliction; they will go into captivity first, since they have turned justice into gall.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how the people in Amos 6 lived and what the LORD says will happen to them?
ev: Describe how the leaders live in 6:4-6
Say what will happen to them in 6:7 and 6:14

nodes.d: Amos is shown locusts and a fire and pleads for Jacob, and the LORD relents; then he is shown a plumbline set in the midst of Israel with the high places and Jeroboam's house to fall.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the three visions of Amos 7:1-9 and how the LORD responds to Amos' prayers?
ev: Say what Amos asks in 7:2 and 7:5 and how the LORD answers
Describe the third vision (7:7-9)

nodes.d: Amaziah priest of Bethel reports Amos to Jeroboam and tells him to flee to Judah; Amos answers that he was a herdman and fig gatherer whom the LORD took and sent, and announces judgment on Amaziah and exile for Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Amaziah said to Amos and how Amos answered?
ev: Retell the exchange
Say how Amos describes his own calling (7:14-15)

nodes.t: Basket of summer fruit; famine of the word
nodes.d: The LORD shows Amos a basket of summer fruit and says the end has come for Israel; Amos charges merchants with cheating and buying the poor, and the LORD announces mourning and a famine of hearing his words.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the famine described in Amos 8:11-12?
ev: Describe the vision and the LORD's explanation (8:1-3)
Name the merchants' sins (8:4-6)
Explain the famine in 8:11-12

nodes.d: The LORD stands by the altar and says none can escape, though they dig to hell or climb to heaven; he will sift Israel among all nations yet not utterly destroy the house of Jacob, and sinners who deny the evil will die.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Amos 9:1-10 shows both the certainty of judgment and a limit placed on it?
ev: Describe how far the LORD's hand reaches in 9:2-4
Read the limit on judgment in 9:8-9

nodes.d: The LORD promises to raise up the fallen tabernacle of David, so that Israel possess the remnant of Edom and the heathen called by his name, with abundant harvests and a restored land from which they will not be uprooted.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the promises that end the book of Amos?
ev: Say what the LORD will raise up (9:11)
Describe the promises of 9:13-15

nodes.d: Acts continues Luke's account from the ascension of Jesus (1:9) to Paul preaching at Rome (28:31): the Holy Ghost at Pentecost, the church in Jerusalem, the witness spreading to Judaea, Samaria and the Gentiles, and Paul's journeys, arrest and voyage to Rome.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline how the gospel spreads in Acts from Jerusalem to Rome?
ev: Say how Acts 1:8 gives the shape of the book (Jerusalem, Judaea, Samaria, the uttermost part)
Name the major sections: Peter in Jerusalem, Stephen and Philip, Saul's conversion, Cornelius, Paul's journeys, Paul's arrest and Rome

nodes.t: Stephen's speech: Moses and the people's refusal
nodes.d: Stephen recounts Israel's growth in Egypt, the birth and upbringing of Moses, his first attempt to help his brethren and their rejection, and God's call from the burning bush. He says the people refused Moses, turned back in their hearts to Egypt, and made a calf.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Stephen says Israel treated Moses, whom God sent as ruler and deliverer?
ev: Retell the stages of Moses' life Stephen names (7:20-36)
Say how Stephen says the fathers treated Moses (7:35, 7:39-41)

nodes.d: Men from Judaea teach that Gentiles must be circumcised to be saved, so Paul and Barnabas go to Jerusalem. Peter recalls God giving the Gentiles the Holy Ghost and says salvation is through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ; James cites the prophets and judges that Gentile believers should not be troubled, only asked to abstain from idols, fornication, strangled things and blood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the question the Jerusalem council settled and how they answered it?
ev: State the question that began the dispute (15:1, 15:5)
Say what Peter and James each concluded (15:7-11, 15:13-19)
